svg.aria-label: How to write с, н: 2 letters, с, н, one after another
svg.title: Writing с, н
svg.desc: 2 letters written one after another: с, н (cyrillic). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansCyrillic-Static.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: с: RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase с demonstration, 07:04–07:08, YouTube, 5 February 2013 <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tqDLDfYoO2o>; н: RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase н demonstration, 05:47–05:52, YouTube, 5 February 2013 <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tqDLDfYoO2o>. Source notes on variation: с: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 07:04–07:08 lowercase с demonstration, the pen begins at the upper right, curves left across the top, descends the left side, sweeps through the bottom, and rises into a small lower-right exit in one continuous counterclockwise pen-down run, for zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated school hand is a tall, slightly slanted open curve with a small rising exit; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a wider, upright printed C-like form with blunt open tips. This learner path preserves the source's upper-right-to-left-side-to-bottom-to-lower-right order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the printed outline as one open counterclockwise curve. Connected cursive may add an entry join and lengthen the source's exit join, and individual handwriting may round, narrow, widen, or slant the open curve differently. н: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 05:47–05:52 lowercase н demonstration, the pen begins at the upper left, descends the left stem to the baseline, turns upward without lifting, crosses through a rounded middle bridge, rises to the right shoulder, descends the right stem, and finishes through a small rising exit in one continuous pen-down run, for zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated school hand has a rounded bridge plus entry and exit joins; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a printed H-like form with two straight vertical stems joined by a horizontal middle bar, without the cursive joins. This learner path preserves the source's left-stem-to-middle-bridge-to-right-stem order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the printed outline: descend the left stem, retrace to the middle junction, sweep through the horizontal bar, rise to the upper-right tip, and descend the right stem without lifting. Connected cursive restores the source's rounded bridge and entry and exit joins, and individual handwriting may round, narrow, or slant the bridge and stems differently.
svg.text: How it is written — 2 letters, one after another
Letter 1 of 2 — one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
Letter 2 of 2 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase с demonstration, 07:04–07:08, YouTube, 5 February
Letter 2: stroke order after RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase н demonstration, 05:47–05:52, YouTube, 5 February
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
